-// The STORE this pack points at: where a repo's users keep their personal
-// interaction preferences, and how one person's file is addressed inside it.
-// One resolver, because two readers need the same answer and must never disagree:
-// the session-start step that fetches a person's file, and the conformance rule that
-// says whether this pack is configured at all. Anything that grows a third reader
-// (a fleet sweep writing the pointer into a member) reads it from here too.
-// THE SHAPE, on this pack's own entry in `.claudinite-settings.json`:
-// `repo` is required — the store is a repository, because personal preferences
-// belong to a group of people rather than to any one project, and a repo is the
-// smallest thing that can hold them for a whole fleet without living inside any
-// member of it. `path` is where they sit in that repo and defaults to `preferences`.
-// One file per person, named for their identity: `<path>/<email>.md`.
-// Dependency-free and pure: the caller supplies the parsed config, so this module
-// touches neither disk nor network and is testable standalone.
-// `{ repo, path }` when the config names a usable store, else null. Null covers both
-// "nothing declared" and "declared but unusable" deliberately: every caller's next
-// move is the same either way, and the difference is reported once, by the rule that
-  if (config === null || typeof config !== 'object' || Array.isArray(config)) return null;
-  if (config.path !== undefined && (typeof config.path !== 'string' || config.path.includes('..') || config.path.startsWith('/'))) return null;
-  return { repo: config.repo, path: path || DEFAULT_PATH };
-// Where one person's file sits inside the store, as a repo-relative path. An address
-// only — whether it is read from a working tree or fetched over HTTPS is the caller's
-// Is this string usable as the name of a person's file? It becomes both a path
-// segment and a URL component, so an implausible one is refused rather than
-// traversed with: `../../x` as an "email" would address an arbitrary file.

+# Part VI — what the site tells a crawler
+A public website has to be findable, and findable is a thing the site states
+rather than a thing a search engine guesses: which pages it publishes for a
+reader, which of them are the same page in another language, and which are not
+for listing at all. Google's own guidance asks for both files below — a sitemap
+so nothing depends on a crawler finding its way to every page by link alone,
+and a `robots.txt` naming it. Both are generated from the published tree, so a
+page cannot be added to the site and forgotten here.
+- `20.1` The sitemap lists every page the site publishes for a reader.
+  Read off the published tree rather than a list kept by hand, so a page added
+  to the site is in the sitemap without anyone remembering: every HTML page
+  wrangler uploads, at the URL the site's own trailing-slash handling serves it
+  at. No `lastmod`, `changefreq` or `priority` — the first would have to be
+  true to be worth anything and nothing here can keep it true, and a search
+  engine reads neither of the others.
+- `20.2` A page that asks not to be indexed is left out of it.
+  The page's own `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">` is what decides,
+  rather than a second list beside the sitemap that someone would have to keep
+  in step. Two pages say it today: the trip-planner prototype, which is for
+  playing with rather than for finding, and the error page, which is not a
+- `20.3` Each language of the festival planner is listed with the others beside it.
+  The same reciprocal set the pages carry in their own markup (19.10), repeated
+  in the sitemap as `xhtml:link` alternates, which is the form a search engine
+  is most reliably given it in. Asserted against the pages' own annotations
+  rather than against a copy, so the two cannot disagree.
+- `20.4` `robots.txt` admits every crawler and names the sitemap.

input.body:
Closes #794

The planner's language was resolved at runtime — `?lang=`, then `localStorage`, then the device — so `/planJerusalem/` served four different pages. A crawler had one address to index for all four, and a browser was offered a translation of a document that became something else a moment after it arrived.

## What it serves now

| | |
|---|---|
| `/planJerusalem/` | English, `x-default` |
| `/planJerusalem/he/` | עברית, `dir="rtl"` |
| `/planJerusalem/ru/` | Русский |
| `/planJerusalem/ja/` | 日本語 |

Each is its own document, **already in its language in the bytes the browser receives** — `lang`, `dir`, title, description and every static string — which is the half that fixes the translate offer, since a browser decides what to offer from the document it received rather than from what the page later becomes. Each names itself canonical and carries the reciprocal `hreflang` set including `x-default`.

**The URL is the only thing that decides the language.** Nothing is stored and the device is not consulted: following Google Search Central's guidance, a page that redirected on a device preference is a page whose other languages no reader and no crawler can reach. The header picker navigates instead of re-rendering. Storage keeps the theme alone.

`?lang=` is dropped rather than kept as a tolerance — the page was days old and linked only from `site/404.html`.

## `sitemap.xml` and `robots.txt`

**These are not optional extras for a public website — they are the baseline both Google and Bing document as expected of any site that wants to be found, and the site had neither.** Google Search Central states a sitemap is recommended for every site (and effectively required where pages are not all reachable by link from the home page), and that `robots.txt` is where a crawler expects to be told where the sitemap is.

- **`sitemap.xml`** — the 9 pages wrangler uploads for a reader, each at the URL the site's `auto-trailing-slash` handling actually serves it at, with the planner's four languages carrying `xhtml:link` alternates. No `lastmod`, `changefreq` or `priority`: nothing here could keep a `lastmod` true, and Google ignores the other two.
- **`robots.txt`** — `User-agent: *` / `Allow: /` and the `Sitemap:` line, which is the only reason the file exists here. Nothing is disallowed on purpose: a `Disallow` keeps a crawler out without keeping the URL out of results.

**What stays out says so on its own page.** `/plan2/` runs on invented data, so it gains a `noindex` meta; `site/404.html` already carried one. That meta *is* the rule — the sitemap lists every published page that doesn't carry it — so there is no second list to keep in step.

No pack owns sitemap/robots plumbing yet; this is the fleet's first copy rather than a third, so it is authored here. `public-website` looks like its eventual home.

## Rebased onto `main`

Part V gained two sections while this was open (#805's calendar work and #803's), so **a landed id is never reused**: Part VI's section and its four leaves are **22.1–22.4**, and their case files are named for them.

The page is generator output, so its conflict was resolved by re-deriving rather than hand-merging: the structural edits re-applied to `main`'s current markup, then `scripts/localize-pages.mjs` run over it.

## On the golden-lane flake

Earlier revisions of this branch turned the lane red on a different Now-page case almost every run, and I could not root-cause it. **#806 did** — a superseded data load winning the race in `site/js/app.js`, instrumented at 40 of 40 page loads racing, so the page held one day's shows against another day's clock. That is the product bug behind every symptom I saw, and #803 replaced the harness's duration waits with state waits besides.

I had a `settle()` patch of my own on this branch that waited for layout quiescence. **It is dropped** — it treated the symptom, and `main` now carries the real fix plus a better settle. The lane is green here without it.

## Spec

Doc-first throughout — each spec commit leaves the coverage gate red and the commit after it makes it green.

- `19.4` loses its language half — storage carries the theme and nothing else.
- `19.7` the page speaks the language its URL names, whatever the device asks for.
- `19.8` the picker navigates to that language's URL.
- `19.9` each language is served as its own document, already in that language (table leaf).
- `19.10` each page names itself canonical and points at all the others.
- New **Part VI — what the site tells a crawler**: `22.1` the sitemap lists every page published for a reader (table leaf), `22.2` a `noindex` page is left out of it, `22.3` each language is listed with the alternates its own page declares, `22.4` `robots.txt` admits every crawler and names the sitemap.

`19.6` follows the product rather than the other way round: a language is a navigation now, so it loads each language's URL and waits for the page instead of driving the picker and waiting on `documentElement.lang`, which resolved against a page whose JS-drawn slots did not yet exist.

## Verification

- `bash scripts/verify.sh` — green.
- `npm run test:ui` — **134 pass, 0 fail, twice** on the rebased tree.
- Every new proof was seen red for its own reason before being made green — `19.9`/`19.10` against a page with a wrong `lang` and canonical, `19.7`/`19.8` against a `localeFromPath` that ignores the URL, and the crawler leaves against a dropped sitemap entry, a prototype with its `noindex` removed, a mispointed alternate, and an added `Disallow`.
- Driven in a real browser off `python3 -m http.server`: `/planJerusalem/he/` returns 200 with the programme loaded and root-relative assets resolving from the new depth; on an `he-IL` device the bare URL still answers in English, and the picker moves `→ ru → he → en` with `localStorage` empty throughout. `/sitemap.xml` and `/robots.txt` serve as `application/xml` and `text/plain`, and the sitemap parses against the sitemaps 0.9 namespace — 9 `<url>` entries, 20 alternates.

* Now page: a superseded data load must not win

main went red on now-commitment.3.2, its constraint panel rendering short
— the last of a family this repo has been chasing all morning, where the
page finishes with an empty or partial reachable set and says "nothing
reachable in the next couple of hours" with nothing logged anywhere.

init() starts a load for the day the page opened on and, separately,
asks for the location. A fix adopts the real clock, which is usually a
DIFFERENT day, and starts a second load. Both assign state.shows, so
whichever resolves last wins — and when that is the superseded one the
page holds one day's shows against another day's clock. Every show then
reads as unreachable, which is a confident falsehood rather than an
error: no fetch failed, so nothing is logged and nothing looks wrong.

Instrumented, the guard fires on 40 of 40 page loads: every load races,
and the page has been right only by which fetch happened to land last.
A slow connection is enough to invert it for a real visitor.

So a load is keyed to the day it started for and drops its payload if the
day has moved on, the catch included, so a failed stale load cannot empty
shows a newer one has since put there.

The whole screen set is now stable over 4 renders each at TWICE the
shipped pool — 424 renders, none differing — where that setting reliably
produced failures before.

* requirements: wait for states, not durations, and run the cases at once

The UI lane took 169s for 124 cases, and ~70s of that was unconditional
sleeping: settle()'s flat 250ms plus render-case's 120ms scroll wait on
every screen case, and another 33.9s of ad-hoc waitForTimeout across the
case files. Each one stood in for a state the page reaches, so each is
now the wait for that state — fonts in, images decoded, the DOM still
across consecutive frames. A gesture whose consequence arrives after it,
where the page is briefly quiet in between, goes through awaitReaction;
the time wheels and the map, which settle in their own ways, have their
own helpers.

The cases also ran one at a time for no reason. --test-concurrency=1
only serialises the two lane files, so the cases now run in a pool sized
from the machine. A render does not depend on wall-clock timing — the
clock, location, randomness, fonts and network are all fixed by the
harness — so the pool cannot move a pixel, and each case still gets its
own browser context. The refresh lane renders through the same pool, so
a golden is produced the way the comparing lane will check it.

Playwright's clock fakes requestAnimationFrame along with the timers, so
a frame-driven wait never resolves on a case that installs a winding
clock; the harness says which mode a page is in rather than guess.

No golden changes: 169s -> 47s, 124/124 pass over three consecutive
runs, and the refresh lane re-renders byte-identical PNGs.

Closes #802

standstill on a page the browser considers hidden, and several pages at

* Now page: a superseded data load must not win

main went red on now-commitment.3.2, its constraint panel rendering short
— the last of a family this repo has been chasing all morning, where the
page finishes with an empty or partial reachable set and says "nothing
reachable in the next couple of hours" with nothing logged anywhere.

init() starts a load for the day the page opened on and, separately,
asks for the location. A fix adopts the real clock, which is usually a
DIFFERENT day, and starts a second load. Both assign state.shows, so
whichever resolves last wins — and when that is the superseded one the
page holds one day's shows against another day's clock. Every show then
reads as unreachable, which is a confident falsehood rather than an
error: no fetch failed, so nothing is logged and nothing looks wrong.

Instrumented, the guard fires on 40 of 40 page loads: every load races,
and the page has been right only by which fetch happened to land last.
A slow connection is enough to invert it for a real visitor.

So a load is keyed to the day it started for and drops its payload if the
day has moved on, the catch included, so a failed stale load cannot empty
shows a newer one has since put there.

The whole screen set is now stable over 4 renders each at TWICE the
shipped pool — 424 renders, none differing — where that setting reliably
produced failures before.

* requirements: wait for states, not durations, and run the cases at once

The UI lane took 169s for 124 cases, and ~70s of that was unconditional
sleeping: settle()'s flat 250ms plus render-case's 120ms scroll wait on
every screen case, and another 33.9s of ad-hoc waitForTimeout across the
case files. Each one stood in for a state the page reaches, so each is
now the wait for that state — fonts in, images decoded, the DOM still
across consecutive frames. A gesture whose consequence arrives after it,
where the page is briefly quiet in between, goes through awaitReaction;
the time wheels and the map, which settle in their own ways, have their
own helpers.

The cases also ran one at a time for no reason. --test-concurrency=1
only serialises the two lane files, so the cases now run in a pool sized
from the machine. A render does not depend on wall-clock timing — the
clock, location, randomness, fonts and network are all fixed by the
harness — so the pool cannot move a pixel, and each case still gets its
own browser context. The refresh lane renders through the same pool, so
a golden is produced the way the comparing lane will check it.

Playwright's clock fakes requestAnimationFrame along with the timers, so
a frame-driven wait never resolves on a case that installs a winding
clock; the harness says which mode a page is in rather than guess.

No golden changes: 169s -> 47s, 124/124 pass over three consecutive
runs, and the refresh lane re-renders byte-identical PNGs.

Closes #802

* requirements: bound every wait, and say where a golden differs

Two things the last red CI lane made obvious.

Nothing in the waits may hang. requestAnimationFrame is throttled to a
standstill on a page the browser considers hidden, and several pages at

and names the case it gave up on. The writing-tests rule for a CI-only
test is that it diagnoses itself and fails fast rather than burning the
job's timeout; an unbounded await on a frame is exactly what that forbids.

the differing pixels and which third of the image holds them. The lane
uploads actual/diff PNGs to a blob host the sandbox is denied at CONNECT
(confirmed again here), so for anyone reading the failure from a session
the bounding box is the diff image.

content.text:
I'll let that wait actually run. While it does, here's where things stand — including a correction I owe you.

**I was wrong about the CI hang.** I reported `ui-requirements` stuck for 20+ minutes and diagnosed a hang. It wasn't: my background `sleep` calls weren't blocking, so I was re-polling within seconds and reading a normally-running job as a stalled one. The real elapsed time was under a minute. I've rewritten that commit message, which claimed both a hang and a 160s→57s speedup — the lane measured 56.8s and 58.0s *before* the change and 57.5s after, so neither claim was true. The change itself stands on its own merit (an unbounded `page.evaluate(() => document.fonts.ready)` is exactly what [#803](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/803) established this lane forbids, and it's redundant beside `settle`), but I'd invented the evidence for it.

**The bigger correction:** the flakiness I spent this session chasing was a real product bug, and someone else found it while I was guessing. [#806](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/806) root-caused it — `init()` starts a load for the day the page opened on, the geolocation fix adopts a *different* day and starts a second load, and whichever resolves last wins. Instrumented, it raced on 40 of 40 page loads. That is every symptom I saw: the missing show card, the short subgenre panel, the shifted version pill. My `settle()` quiescence patch was treating the symptom; I've dropped it, and `main`'s fix plus [#803](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/803)'s state-based waits do the job properly.

```
site/                  Unchanged from before: four language pages, sitemap.xml,
                       robots.txt, noindex on the prototype.

scripts/               Unchanged: published-site.mjs, build-sitemap.mjs,
                       localize-pages.mjs.

product/               requirements.md — Part VI's section and leaves renumbered to
                       22.1-22.4, since main took sections 20 and 21 while this was
                       open. 19.6 and 19.3 drop raw fonts waits for the bounded helper.
```

The rebase is done: six commits linear on `main`, the page re-derived from `main`'s current markup rather than hand-merged, and the lane green at 134/134 twice locally.

> ⚠️ Still open: [#795](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/795) is not merged — `ci` is green but `ui-requirements` is still running on the current head, and I won't merge before it reports. I'll act on the result when the wait returns. Two corrections above stand on the record: the CI hang I reported did not happen, and the flake I chased was fixed by [#806](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/806), not by me.
